text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Pay-related bonus lacks recorded review","detail":"A referral bonus is driver compensation, a policy-controlled area (pay). Legal review is described as waived via a VP email with no ticket, which is not a recorded review.","evidence_quote":"Legal review: waived per VP email, no ticket.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record the required legal/compensation policy review with a ticket and approval, rather than relying on an informal waiver."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Switchback design with insufficient and misaligned duration","detail":"A 4-week switchback by market-week gives few cycles and risks carryover: referred drivers recruited in one week persist into later control weeks. The bonus requires 50 deliveries for payout and the target window is 10 weeks, so 4 weeks cannot observe the effect. Also, a referral program's effect on driver supply is not a market-week-reversible treatment.","evidence_quote":"Switchback by market-week. Duration: 4 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use a geo/market-level randomized or staggered rollout design with a unit that does not leak between arms, and a duration long enough to observe referred drivers completing 50 deliveries and affecting acceptance."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No guardrails for fraud or driver quality from referral incentives","detail":"The proposal changes pay incentives and driver onboarding but lacks guardrails on referral fraud/self-referral, new driver quality or on-time delivery, and customer experience. Existing guardrails don't cover these risks.","evidence_quote":"Driver Safety Incident Rate: stop if it rises more than 5% over baseline.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as on-time delivery rate, referral fraud/abuse rate, new-driver 30-day retention, and customer-reported delivery quality."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric doesn't match the stated problem","detail":"The problem is driver supply shortage, but the success metric is Driver Acceptance Rate, which does not measure supply growth or new-driver onboarding. The stated link between the referral bonus and acceptance rate is unclear and the metric is ambiguous for this purpose.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate: baseline 71%, target 75% within 10 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use a defined supply metric (e.g., new active drivers activated per market, or supply-hours coverage) as primary, with acceptance rate as secondary if justified."}]}
